memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'Throughout the land that you hold as a possession, you must provide for
the redemption of the land. If one of your fellow Israelites becomes poor
and sells some of their property, their nearest relative is to come and
redeem what they have sold'" - Lev 25:24-25 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God built a rescue mechanism into Israel's law. If poverty forced someone
to sell their land, a near relative could step in, pay the price, and buy
it back for them. This relative was called the kinsman-redeemer.

Notice the two things required of this redeemer. He had to be a relative —
near enough in family to have the right to act. And he had to be willing
and able to pay the cost. Family connection plus willing sacrifice brought
redemption.

Dear reader, this quiet legal provision is one of the loveliest signposts
to Christ in the whole Old Testament. We had lost our inheritance. We had
sold ourselves into slavery to sin and could not buy ourselves back. We
needed a kinsman-redeemer.

And so the Son of God became one of us. Hebrews says He shared in our
humanity so that He might free us (Heb 2:14-15). He became our near
relative, our brother, in order to have the right to redeem. And He paid
the price with His own blood.

The story of Ruth shows this beautifully, where Boaz redeems Ruth and
restores her family line. Paul says Christ redeemed us from the curse of
the law by becoming a curse for us (Gal 3:13).

You could not buy yourself back. Your Redeemer did it for you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I grasp that I could never have redeemed myself?
2. What does it mean that Jesus became my near relative to rescue me?
3. How does being redeemed at such cost change how I live?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord Jesus, thank You for becoming one of us and paying the price to buy me
back. I could never have redeemed myself. All my gratitude belongs to You.
Amen.
